docs.html:
Tier key: C Core — whiteboard-fluent · I Important — concept + tradeoffs · B Breadth — recognize & place

1 — Framing the Agentic Round

  • C Do we need an agent at all? — single call → workflow → single agent → multi-agent; start at the lowest rung that fits. This question is graded.
  • C Clarifying questions that change the design — how open-ended the task is, whether actions can be undone, latency class (interactive / async / batch), stakes, who checks the output
  • C Autonomy level as a requirement — assist → supervised → autonomous, set by how reversible the action is × what a mistake costs, not by ambition
  • C Metrics before boxes — task success rate, pass^k, cost/task, steps/task, escalation rate, p95 time-to-complete
  • I Is there a verifier? — tests, SQL results, schema checks (strong) vs none (support, research); this one fact shapes the whole architecture
  • B 45-minute pacing for agent prompts — use the MICRO preset in ../00-Index/ai_design_prompt_v4.md

Depth → agentic #1–8 (spectrum, agents vs workflows, autonomy, when not to build) · RAG index #43

2 — Reference Architecture

  • C The layers — gateway → orchestrator/runtime → model router → tool layer → memory & state → guardrails → observability
  • C Agent = model + harness; the harness (loop, tools, context, checks) is where the design lives
  • C Control flow vs side effects — the loop decides, the tool layer acts; keep authority out of the loop
  • I Sync vs async runs — request/response for runs under ~30s; job ID + stream/webhook/poll for anything longer
  • I Deterministic code wrapping the LLM — the model as one step in a workflow, not the owner of the flow
  • B Managed runtimes — Bedrock Agents, Vertex Agent Builder, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK — and where each fits in the layers

Depth → agentic #7, #91, #110 · 05-LLM-Production/13-Evals-Practice/06-Harness Engineering

3 — Control Flow & Orchestration

  • C Workflow patterns before agents — prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer
  • C ReAct vs Plan-and-Execute vs ReWOO — adaptivity vs predictability vs token cost; loop drift vs brittle plans
  • C Explicit state machine / graph orchestration — bounded loops, named termination conditions, testable transitions
  • I Reflection / critic loops — worth it only when the critique can be checked; otherwise it doubles cost for a vibe
  • I Framework vs plain SDK; graph-based vs role-based vs code-first orchestration
  • B Reasoning models as planners — fewer steps, slower steps; ToT/GoT as search when budget allows

Depth → agentic #3–4, #10–19, #58–64

4 — Tool Layer Design

  • C Tools are an API contract — task-level granularity (not raw CRUD), clear names, JSON Schema, error messages written so the model can recover
  • C Validate at the boundary — arguments checked in code; structured output / constrained decoding; never execute raw model output
  • C Read tools vs write tools — writes are idempotent (idempotency keys), scoped, and gated separately
  • I Tool selection at scale — 50+ tools → tool retrieval, namespacing, per-agent toolsets
  • I Parallel tool calls — the biggest latency lever, and a race on any shared state
  • I MCP as the integration layer — host/client/server, transports, build vs consume servers; B A2A for agent-to-agent; OpenAPI → tools
  • I Code execution (CodeAct) and computer/browser use — richer action space in exchange for a mandatory sandbox and flaky runs
  • I Human-as-a-tool — escalation/approval as a callable action with a typed payload

Depth → agentic #20–36

5 — Memory, State & Context

  • C Three stores, three lifetimes — working context (per step) · thread state (checkpointer, per run/session) · long-term memory (across sessions, per user)
  • C Context engineering is a budget — what enters the window each step: compaction, summarization, trimming tool results, just-in-time retrieval
  • C Context rot & poisoning — long runs degrade; fix with sub-agent context isolation and fresh-context restarts
  • I Long-term memory pipeline — extract → consolidate → read by relevance + recency → forget; strict per-user isolation
  • I Agentic RAG — retrieval as a tool, multi-hop, self-correcting re-retrieval; know when a fixed RAG pipeline is enough
  • I Shared state across agents — blackboard vs message passing; concurrent writes to shared memory
  • B Backends (vector / KV / graph) and frameworks (Mem0, Zep, Letta)

Depth → agentic #37–47, #66–71 · 08-Prompt-engineering §5 (context budgeting)

6 — Multi-Agent Topology

  • C Single vs multi-agent — justify with work that splits into parallel parts or needs isolated context, never with "roles look tidy"
  • C Orchestrator-worker (lead + sub-agents) — the production default; delegation contract = objective, output format, tools, effort budget
  • C Cost & error multiplication — a single agent uses ~4× the tokens of chat, multi-agent ~15× (Anthropic research-system figures); errors compound across handoffs
  • I Topologies — sequential, hierarchical supervisor, handoff/swarm, network; B group chat / round-robin
  • I Coordination failures — duplicated work, conflicting writes, context lost at handoff, sub-agents that never finish
  • B Debate / critique ensembles — quality via disagreement, at N× cost

Depth → agentic #48–57 · scenario Design-Multi-Agent-Workflow

7 — Durable Execution & Long-Running Runs

  • C Checkpoint every step, resume after a crash — a workflow-engine problem (Temporal, Step Functions, LangGraph checkpointer), and saying so is a differentiator
  • C Partial completion & orphaned side effects — record created, email never sent → saga/compensation, idempotency, outbox for exactly-once effects
  • C HITL as a durable pause — hours or days, state persisted, resume with the approval payload
  • I Queues & workers for async agents — backpressure, per-tenant concurrency limits, priority lanes
  • I Cancellation & timeouts — wall-clock budgets; a user abort must reach in-flight tool calls
  • I Replay / time travel from a checkpoint — debugging and "fork from step N"

Depth → agentic #45, #62, #97 · HLD §§6–7 (outbox, saga, idempotency)

8 — Reliability Engineering

  • C Compounding error — p^N: 0.95^10 ≈ 0.60; the case for fewer steps and verification gates
  • C Hard budgets — step cap, token cap, wall-clock cap, loop detection on repeated identical calls
  • C Retries with backoff at the model and tool layers — safe only with idempotent tools; watch for retry storms
  • C Model fallback, provider failover, a circuit breaker per tool and per provider
  • I Verification gates — deterministic checks first (schema, tests, execution), critic model last
  • I Graceful degradation — fall back to a fixed workflow, a partial answer, or a human
  • I pass@k vs pass^k — reliability means consistency across runs, not the best single run

Depth → agentic #8, #78, #92 · 13-Evals-Practice/02 · Failure-Modes index #85–93

9 — Latency & Streaming

  • C Latency ≈ Σ steps (prefill + decode + tool time) — the multiplication problem; prefill grows as context accumulates
  • C Levers — fewer steps, parallel tools, a smaller model per step, prefix caching, plan once then execute
  • C Stream progress, not just tokens — tool-call events, status, partial results; perceived latency ≠ total latency
  • I Real-time / voice agents — STT → LLM → TTS within a sub-second turn budget, barge-in, turn-taking, interruption cancels in-flight tools
  • I Transport — SSE vs WebSocket vs WebRTC for agent streams

Depth → agentic #65, #93, #99, #106 · 01-Networking (transport)

10 — Cost Modeling & Optimization

  • C cost ≈ Σ steps (input tokens × input price + output tokens × output price) — context is re-billed every step, so cost grows roughly with steps²
  • C Model routing / cascades — small model for routing and extraction, frontier model only for planning and hard steps
  • C Caching tiers — prefix/prompt caching (put static content first), tool-result caching, semantic caching (unsafe for actions)
  • C Spend caps per run and per tenant, enforced in the gateway — never in the prompt
  • I Unit economics — cost per successful task, token attribution per feature
  • I Batch APIs for async agents; self-host vs API break-even 📐

Depth → agentic #88, #94–95 · RAG index #65–66, #96

11 — Safety, Security & Governance

  • C Indirect prompt injection — instructions arrive through tool results and retrieved docs; the lethal trifecta = private data + untrusted content + a way to send data out
  • C Least privilege — per-tool scoped credentials, acting on behalf of the user (delegated OAuth), the confused-deputy problem
  • C Sandboxing — isolated containers/microVMs for code, allowlisted network egress, filesystem boundaries
  • C Approval gates on irreversible actions — and an audit of the tool graph for any path that skips the gate
  • I Guardrails — input / output / action rails; a policy engine outside the model
  • I Audit trail — every prompt, tool call, argument, result and approver, kept for compliance
  • I Multi-tenant isolation — memory, tool credentials, traces, caches
  • B OWASP LLM Top 10 and agentic threat modeling

Depth → agentic #81–90 · RAG index #71–72

12 — Evaluation & Observability

  • C Why agent eval is different — trajectories, non-determinism, real side effects
  • C Layered eval — tool-call accuracy & argument validity → step success → trajectory → end-to-end task success
  • C Tracing is a requirement — a span per step and tool call, tokens and cost per step (OpenTelemetry GenAI, LangSmith, Langfuse)
  • C Evals in CI — a regression gate on every prompt, tool, model or graph change
  • I LLM-as-judge on trajectories — rubric-based, with position/verbosity/self-preference controls
  • I Simulation & replay — sandboxed environments, recorded tool responses, simulated users
  • I Online eval — escalation rate and human edits as labels
  • B Benchmarks — SWE-bench, τ-bench, GAIA, WebArena: what they do and don't predict

Depth → agentic #72–80 · 05-LLM-Production/13-Evals-Practice · scenario Design-LLM-Eval-Pipeline

13 — Deployment, Versioning & Scaling

  • C Version prompts + tools + model + graph together — one coupled artifact; pin model versions
  • I Rollout — shadow runs, canary judged on task success, feature flags, fast rollback
  • I Scaling — stateless workers with state stored outside them, long-lived connections, queue-driven autoscaling
  • I Provider rate limits — token buckets per provider/model, priority queues, reserved capacity
  • I Build vs buy — managed agent platform vs custom runtime

Depth → agentic #96, #98, #100–101

14 — Canonical Agentic Design Problems

  • C Coding agent — plan → edit → test loop; tests as the verifier; sandbox; repo-map context (agentic #103)
  • C Support agent that takes actions (refunds, account changes) — no verifier → confidence-based escalation, approval thresholds (#104, RAG #86)
  • C Deep research agent — lead + parallel searchers, citation aggregation, step/cost caps (#70, #105, RAG #91)
  • C Data / SQL analyst agent — schema grounding, read-only role, query cost caps, ambiguity handling (#108, RAG #88)
  • I Voice / interview agent — turn latency budget, barge-in, separate conduct from evaluation (#106–107)
  • I Back-office workflow automation — agent vs RPA vs hybrid, HITL checkpoints (#109)
  • I Browser / computer-use agent — action space, sandbox, flaky UIs (#27)
  • I Internal agent platform for many teams — MCP gateway/tool registry, tenancy, shared eval & tracing
  • C "Our agent succeeds 60% of the time and costs too much — fix it" 📐 — trace → classify failures → cut steps → add verifiers → route models

Rehearse → GenAI Scenario Bank · write new problems with ai_design_prompt_v4.md (MACRO preset)

15 — Architect Lens (staff / architect rounds)

  • C Autonomy vs reliability vs cost/latency — name the tradeoff out loud and justify where you land
  • C Debugging a failing agent — trace first, then classify: planning, tool, context, or model failure
  • C No new physics — saga, outbox, idempotency, circuit breaker, backpressure map one-to-one onto agents; lead with the backend framing
  • I Ownership — who owns tool contracts, eval sets, and on-call for an agent in production
  • I Growth path — how the design changes at 10×: more tools, more tenants, longer runs

Depth → agentic #102 · Failure-Modes index §6 · master index §4

Study order

  1. §1–2 — framing + reference architecture. Every agentic round opens with "do we need an agent?" and a box diagram.
  2. §3–4 — control flow and tools. The mechanics asked in every follow-up.
  3. §7–8 — durable execution and reliability. Where the backend background wins — take these before multi-agent.
  4. §6 — multi-agent, with the cost and error math ready to argue against it.
  5. §9–10 — latency and cost. Have one number for each ready before any mock.
  6. §11–12 — security and eval. The architect differentiators; weave them into every design instead of saving them for the end.
  7. §5, §13 — memory/context and deployment, as follow-up armour.
  8. §14 — rehearse coding, support, research and SQL agents out loud, 45 minutes each; §15 throughout.

Depth rule

This file creates no topic notes — every C/I item already has a depth note under 03-Agentic-AI. C means you can draw it, give one number, and name one failure mode without notes. I means you can state the tradeoff in two sentences. B means you can place it in one line. New writing goes into §14 design problems (AI-HLD template), not into new concept notes.
